primary_source.citation: Finn RS, Brims FJH, Gandhi A, et al. Radiological evaluation of malignant pleural mesothelioma — defining distant metastatic disease. BMC Cancer. 2020;20:1200.
primary_source.study_type: Retrospective single-centre Phase I referral cohort; n=164 advanced MPM patients

biomarkers.name: BAP1
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic (distinguishes malignant mesothelioma from reactive mesothelial proliferations); germline BAP1 mutations define a tumour predisposition syndrome

biomarkers.name: MTAP / CDKN2A (p16) loss
biomarkers.clinical_use: Diagnostic marker (loss supports malignancy); CDKN2A homozygous deletion is common in pleural mesothelioma and MTAP loss often co-occurs; potential MAT2A/PRMT5 targetable pathway

biomarkers.name: NF2
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common tumour suppressor alteration in MPM; predictive utility remains unproven clinically, although NF2-deficient disease has been explored in FAK/Hippo-pathway targeted trials

biomarkers.name: Calretinin, WT1, CK5/6, D2-40 (podoplanin)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Mesothelial lineage markers — distinguish from adenocarcinoma

biomarkers.name: Claudin-4, MOC-31, CEA, Ber-EP4
biomarkers.prevalence: Negative in mesothelioma; positive in adenocarcinoma
biomarkers.clinical_use: Negative markers supporting mesothelial vs epithelial origin

biomarkers.name: PD-L1 (TPS or CPS)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Nivolumab + ipilimumab first-line unresectable MPM (CheckMate 743) — benefit greatest in non-epithelioid, though approved regardless of PD-L1

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A
biomarkers.clinical_use: One of the hallmark genomic alterations in pleural mesothelioma; supports malignant mesothelioma over reactive mesothelial proliferation and is generally associated with worse prognosis

biomarkers.name: SETD2, LATS2, TP53
biomarkers.prevalence: Recurrent but less common than BAP1/CDKN2A/NF2
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recognised recurrent tumour suppressor alterations in MPM; mainly of biologic and research significance rather than routine clinical biomarker use

biomarkers.name: ALK fusion
biomarkers.prevalence: Rare; mainly reported in a small subset of younger peritoneal mesotheliomas rather than typical pleural MPM
biomarkers.clinical_use: Rare actionable driver fusion; not a hallmark driver of pleural mesothelioma

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Diffuse pleural thickening with 'rind' encasing the lung; tubulopapillary, solid, or sarcomatoid architecture
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Nuclear grade for epithelioid MPM (2-tier: low vs high) is prognostic

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: Variable — sarcomatoid subtype more inflamed and IO-responsive than epithelioid
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Extensive fibrous reaction; asbestos bodies in adjacent lung parenchyma

cellular_states_and_lineage.developmental_lineage: Mesoderm — lateral plate mesoderm (splanchnopleuric layer forms serosal surfaces)
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Epithelioid retains mesothelial differentiation (calretinin+, WT1+, D2-40+); sarcomatoid represents EMT with mesenchymal features; biphasic combines both
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Epithelioid → sarcomatoid progression represents EMT within same clonal population; asbestos-induced chronic inflammation drives lineage instability
